business-data-context

Business data map

Entities, relationships, state machines, automatic processes, integrations and the flows that move data. Target system: upex-bunkai-tms (Next.js 15 + Supabase monolith).

Overview

Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System (TMS) for QA teams. A Workspace is the tenant boundary and the commercial unit (plan community | cloud | enterprise). Inside it, Projects hold a self-referential Module tree (max depth 6, materialized path) whose nodes anchor the product's test surface: User Stories carry ordered Acceptance Criteria, and the core artifact — the ATC (Atomic Test Component) — is a mandatory-FK anchor to project, module and story, with an execution layer (UI | API | Unit), an optional test-design technique and priority, ordered steps and assertions, tags (max 10) and an optimistic-lock version.

A second artifact family, Tests, chains existing ATCs into ordered, workspace-scoped suites — a Test is a view over ATCs, not a copy. What actually executes is a Run: at creation the whole chain is snapshotted into immutable run_atcs/run_steps rows, step verdicts progress through a pending/passed/failed/blocked/skipped machine, and the Run terminates as passed | failed | aborted. Failures become native Bugs (severity P1–P4, forward-only lifecycle open → in_progress → resolved → closed) whose provenance rows (run, run step, ATC) are frozen at filing and ON DELETE SET NULL when upstream content is purged.

Everything that matters is appended to an activity log whose AFTER INSERT triggers fan out into a per-recipient notifications inbox (in-app, 90-day visibility, idempotent per source event), plus a daily 08:00 UTC email digest claimed through notification_digest_log. Commercial and lifecycle concerns bracket the tenant: Stripe checkout upgrades a workspace to the cloud plan (project limits 3 → 50 via a DB trigger; seat metadata in purchased_seats), workspace exports build archives into Supabase Storage with a 168-hour expiry, and workspace deletion follows a 30-day soft-delete grace with restore, then a nightly pg_cron purge that leaves a workspace_deletions tombstone outliving the tenant row.

Auth is dual-mode — browser session (Supabase Auth cookies: password, magic link, OAuth GitHub/Google) and personal access tokens (PATs) for CLI/agents — and both collapse to a single Principal; Postgres RLS plus SECURITY DEFINER RPCs enforce authorization. PAT issuance is browser-session-only (a PAT cannot mint another PAT). External integrations: Jira (one-way story import worker), Stripe (hosted checkout + signed webhook), Resend (digest and deletion-notice emails, sent from app code — Postgres has no egress), Vercel (hosting, cron, after() background workers) and Supabase (Postgres 16, Auth, Realtime on run_atcs/run_steps, Storage bucket workspace-exports).

Actors: QA engineers author ATCs/Tests and execute Runs; developers and product owners refine stories and ACs; workspace owners handle billing, members and deletion; automated executors (human / agent / ci) produce Run results; CLI agents act through PATs. Overview figures deferred (see discovery-gaps).

Entities

The spine is workspaces → projects → modules → user_stories → acceptance_criteria → atcs. The module tree is the product's geography; every requirement, ATC and bug anchors to a module. Execution is detached from authoring: Tests chain ATCs, and Runs snapshot into run_atcs/run_steps so test history survives ATC edits. Quality records (bugs with frozen provenance, activity-log-driven notifications, milestones/test-plans as planning objects) and the commercial/lifecycle layer (billing, exports, deletion) complete the model. All tables below were verified against supabase/migrations/ on 2026-10-10.

Entity Business role Why it exists
auth.users Identity (Supabase Auth) Password + email-verification sign-up, magic link and OAuth GitHub/Google; phone auth disabled. One identity feeds browser sessions and PAT issuance.
workspaces Multi-tenant boundary + commercial unit Carries the plan (community | cloud | enterprise), owner_user_id, globally unique kebab-case slug and the deleted_at grace clock. Everything below is scoped to it.
workspace_members RBAC membership Who can see/do what inside a tenant. Role viewer | member | admin | owner; status active | invited | suspended (only active passes RLS). The owner's last-member exit is blocked.
workspace_invites + workspace_invite_secrets Pending membership, 7-day TTL Roles viewer | member | admin only — ownership is transferred, never invited. Raw invite token isolated in the secrets companion table (0011).
projects System-under-test container Bounded per plan by a DB trigger (community = 3, cloud = 50, enterprise = unlimited; SQLSTATE 45700) — monetization limits live in Postgres, not app code.
modules Hierarchical taxonomy of the product Self-referential tree, max depth 6 via CHECK on the materialized path, archived_at soft delete. The archive cascade function soft-deletes descendant modules, stories, ACs and ATCs (not tests or bugs).
user_stories Business requirement unit draft → ready_to_test gate (needs ≥1 active AC). Carries Jira link columns external_id/external_url; one active story per (project_id, upper(external_id)). Soft-archiveable.
acceptance_criteria Testable condition of a story Positioned list inside a story. Archiving the last active AC reverts the parent story to draft inside the SECURITY DEFINER archive RPC (not a table trigger — see discovery-gaps).
atcs CORE artifact — one reusable, atomic test case Layer UI | API | Unit (required), optional technique/priority (0087), tags (≤10), version optimistic lock, tsv search. project_id, module_id and user_story_id are all mandatory FKs. atcs.status exists (CHECK pass|fail|blocked|skipped|running|unrun) but is a dead column with no production writer — live verdicts come from run_atcs.
atc_steps / atc_assertions Ordered executable detail of an ATC Separate ordered lists (unique(atc_id, position) each); assertions are what a run step actually evaluates.
atc_acceptance_criteria AC ↔ ATC traceability (M:N) Feeds coverage and traceability reports — the “is this AC covered?” answer.
tests + test_steps Executable suite = ordered ATC chain Workspace-scoped: they can chain ATCs from any project in the workspace. version optimistic lock, tags text[], title 1–200. Chain positions are unique(test_id, position); FK to ATCs is RESTRICT; deliberately no unique(test_id, atc_id) — the same ATC may appear twice.
project_environments Execution target unique(project_id, lower(name)); “Staging” and “Production” seeded once for projects existing at migration 0031 — new projects get no environments automatically (writes are default-deny; env management was a future story).
runs One execution of a Test Status running | passed | failed | aborted (inserted already running — no created state), executor_mode human | agent | ci, 24h idempotency on (test_id, start_token), optional module_id, denormalized workspace_id/project_id/test_title, optimistic-lock version, abort_reason constrained coherent with aborted.
run_atcs Per-ATC snapshot + computed verdict inside a run Realtime-published (0043 adds it to supabase_realtime). Verdict is recomputed from steps on every mark: any pending → pending; else any failed → failed; else any blocked → blocked; else passed; terminal finish force-skips leftovers.
run_steps Per-step immutable snapshot + evidence Status pending | passed | failed | blocked | skipped. Content copied at run creation so later ATC edits never rewrite history. Realtime-published; keyed by run_atc_id (no direct run_id column).
test_plans + test_plan_tests Named release-scoped test plan (M:N to tests) Project-scoped (0073): unique (project_id, lower(name)). Status open | closed. SELECT-only RLS; all writes via ADR-0012 SECURITY DEFINER RPCs with no caller-supplied actor. Delete is permanently absent — Close is the sole exit.
bugs Native defect record Severity P1–P4, forward-only status open → in_progress → resolved → closed. Title trimmed 5–200, ≤10 evidence URLs. Provenance (run_id, run_step_id, atc_id) frozen at filing with ON DELETE SET NULL; module_id always set. Never archived — the bug table only grows.
milestones Project target-date marker Name 1–100, optional description ≤500, target_date within today…+5y (bounds re-checked only when the date changes). No status, no completion, no deletion — date markers by design.
activity_log Append-only audit trail Source of truth for “who did what”; AFTER INSERT triggers fan out to notifications. Reads go through allowlisted RPCs, not raw table selects.
notifications Per-recipient in-app inbox Payload snapshot (title/type/entity ids), idempotent on (source_event_id, recipient), 90-day visibility window, Realtime-published, no DELETE policy (purge job out of scope in migrations).
notification_preferences Global opt-out per user event_type (run_lifecycle | bug_lifecycle | mentions) × channel (in_app | email); mentions is locked-on. Race-safe upsert with WHERE clause (0062).
notification_digest_log Email-digest claim ledger One row per user per day (pending → sent | failed) — the DB-side idempotency that stops double emails from cron retries.
access_tokens + access_token_secrets Personal Access Token for CLI/agents Raw secret isolated in a companion table (0011/0086); issuance only through a browser session; revoked on workspace deletion/member exit.
billing_checkout_sessions One Stripe Checkout attempt target_plan ∈ ('cloud'), seat_quantity > 0, partial unique one-open-per-workspace, Stripe session id unique-but-nullable; owner-SELECT-only RLS (writes via service-role RPC).
stripe_webhook_events Webhook replay fence PK = Stripe event id → duplicate deliveries become no-ops. No FKs; RLS enabled with zero policies = service-role only.
workspace_exports Tenant data archive job queued | running | completed | failed, expires_at = completed_at + 168h; archive lands in Storage bucket workspace-exports. Owner + cookie-session only; one active export at a time.
workspace_deletions Tombstone outliving the tenant No status column: state is derived from purge_deadline/purged_at. Captures member_count + row_count_digest for compliance. RLS enabled with zero policies — only SECURITY DEFINER RPCs touch it. No FK to workspaces, so it survives the purge.
import_jobs Async Jira import unit queued | running | completed | failed; progress cursor consumed by the UI poller.
idempotency_keys HTTP retry safety pending | succeeded | failed; keyed per workspace+route so a retried POST never double-applies (distinct from Run start_token domain idempotency).
feature_flags, user_view_state, magic_link_tokens + secrets Support tables Per-workspace feature toggles (runtime usage untraced), per-user UI view preferences, and single-use TTL-bound passwordless sign-in tokens with the raw token in a secrets companion (0011/0086).

Key relationships (why they exist). Workspace owns everything by scope; membership gates it via RLS. A module is the geographic anchor: stories, ATCs and bugs all resolve to one, and bugs keep module_id mandatory so module history stays answerable after upstream content is gone. Stories hold ACs; ATCs anchor to story (mandatory) and to ACs through the M:N join — this is the structural traceability the product sells. Tests reference ATCs by pointer (RESTRICT keeps in-use ATCs undeletable); Runs freeze that chain at start so metrics never drift. Bug provenance points back into a Run but degrades to NULL rather than blocking cleanup. Notifications are a presentation layer over the activity log, never a second source of truth.

Entity: ATC (core artifact)

The ATC is the reuse primitive: instead of copying steps between monolithic test cases, teams write one ATC and chain it into many Tests. Three mechanisms make that safe:

  • Mandatory anchoring. project_id, module_id and user_story_id are NOT NULL FKs — an unanchored test component cannot exist in the database, which is how the product enforces “structural traceability” as a schema invariant rather than a convention. AC binding is a separate M:N join (atc_acceptance_criteria) used by coverage reports.
  • Optimistic locking. Every edit carries the expected version; the update RPC bumps it atomically and a stale version is rejected (409 family). Two editors cannot silently clobber each other.
  • Dead status column. atcs.status has a CHECK (pass|fail|blocked|skipped|running|unrun — note the non-past-tense forms, unlike run statuses) but no production writer. Migration 0050 moved coverage reports to read run_atcs verdicts instead. Any new report that reads atcs.status is a bug; the business answer to “does this ATC pass?” always comes from run history.
  • Classification (0087). technique is nullable, constrained to Equivalence Partitioning | Boundary Value Analysis | State Transition | Decision Table | Pairwise; priority is nullable, constrained to Critical | High | Medium | Low. NULL means “not specified” — neither field is ever defaulted.
  • Search. A trigger keeps a tsvector (search_vector) in sync from title/tags, powering /atcs/search without app-side indexing.

Deletion is ON DELETE RESTRICT against test_steps: an ATC that sits in any Test chain cannot be deleted until removed from those chains (the usage endpoint reports where it is referenced). Archive is soft (archived_at).

Entity: Tests (ATC chains)

A Test is an ordered list of ATC references, not a copy of their content. That single decision has three consequences QA depends on:

  • Edit propagation. Changing an ATC's steps immediately changes every Test that chains it — because the chain stores pointers, and because Runs snapshot instead (see entity-run-snapshots). This is why the ATC reuse ratio metric works at all.
  • Workspace scope. Tests live at workspace level, so a suite can chain ATCs from several projects (cross-project release suites). They are not children of a project.
  • Positional uniqueness only. unique(test_id, position) orders the chain; there is deliberately no unique(test_id, atc_id), so the same ATC may appear at multiple positions (repeat-verification scenarios are legal). FK to atcs is RESTRICT — you cannot delete an ATC that any chain still references.

Reorder is a single-transaction rewrite of all positions behind the version optimistic lock; tags are a text[] column trimmed/deduped app-side; title is trimmed to 1–200 chars.

Entity: Runs (snapshot model)

A Run is the immutable record of one execution. At creation the RPC copies every chain test_steps row into run_steps (content frozen) and creates one run_atcs shell per chain ATC with status = pending. Later edits to the Test or its ATCs never rewrite this history — this is the whole reason runs snapshot instead of referencing live content.

  • Computed, never authored, ATC verdicts. run_atcs.status is recomputed inside the step-mark RPC on every mark: any step pending → pending; else any failed → failed; else any blocked → blocked; else passed. It is never an independent write target.
  • Terminal guards. Once a Run leaves running, every later finish/abort/mark is rejected (SQLSTATE 45204 abort / 45206 finish / 45212 mark). First terminal state wins; history is immutable.
  • Idempotent start. The same (test_id, start_token) within a 24h window returns the existing Run instead of creating a second one — CLI/agents retry network calls, and a retry must not spawn a second execution. This is domain-level and separate from the generic idempotency_keys table.
  • Module snapshot. An optional module_id is captured at creation so module-scoped rollups stay stable even if the Test's association changes later.
  • Realtime. run_atcs and run_steps are added to the supabase_realtime publication (0043); the client subscribes with a two-binding filter (run_id on run_atcs, run_atc_id in (...) on run_steps, since run_steps has no direct run_id column).

Entity: Notifications (inbox semantics)

Notifications are a read model over the activity log, never a second source of truth. Key semantics:

  • Idempotent fan-out. Rows are unique on (source_event_id, recipient), so trigger re-fires and retries can never double-notify.
  • Snapshot payload. Title/type/entity ids are copied at insert; later renames do not rewrite inbox history. An availability flag marks rows whose target was since deleted.
  • 90-day visibility. The list RPC filters created_at >= now() - interval '90 days'; older rows drop out of listing (storage hygiene) but are not hard-deleted by any migration path observed.
  • Preferences are global per user (not per workspace): event_type × channel, with mentions locked on — being mentioned always notifies (product decision). The preference upsert uses a WHERE-clause race guard (0062).
  • Realtime updates the unread badge live (the table is in the supabase_realtime publication per the notifications migration).

Entity: Access tokens (PAT secret split)

Personal Access Tokens authenticate CLI/agent traffic (Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_…). The raw secret lives in a companion table (access_token_secrets), not on the token row: migration 0011 split secrets out, and 0086 revoked the read-only QA inspector role's access to every *_secrets companion (access-token, magic-link, invite). Lookup is by prefix index then constant-time hash compare; a user JWT is minted so RLS auth.uid() applies identically to the cookie rail. Issuance exists only behind a browser session — a PAT cannot mint another PAT (privilege-escalation wall). Tokens are revoked when the member leaves a workspace or the workspace is deleted (same transaction as the removal — no window where tokens outlive intent).

Entity: Billing checkout (one-open, event-fenced)

Two constraints make Stripe retries and double-clicks safe at the schema level:

  • One open attempt per workspace. A partial unique index on (workspace_id) WHERE status = 'open' means a second checkout click gets 409 instead of creating a second Stripe session. target_plan is constrained to ('cloud') — upgrade only; there is no subscription lifecycle table (one-shot state change, per-seat metadata in purchased_seats).
  • Event-id replay fence. stripe_webhook_events uses the Stripe event id as primary key: a duplicate delivery conflicts and becomes an immediate 200 no-op. The table has RLS enabled with zero policies — only service-role code writes it.

Plan limits are enforced by the bunkai_enforce_project_limit_trigger (BEFORE INSERT on projects, SQLSTATE 45700): community = 3, cloud = 50, enterprise = unlimited. The DB mirrors of lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts are authoritative — no app deployment can forget the limit. Seat count is display metadata; invite-time seat enforcement does not exist yet.

Entity: Workspace deletions (tombstone)

The tombstone deliberately outlives the tenant. It has no foreign key to workspaces, no status column (state is derived: purged_at IS NULL means awaiting purge) and RLS enabled with zero policies, so only SECURITY DEFINER RPCs can touch it. It captures member_count and a row_count_digest at request time for compliance (“what did this tenant contain?”) — answers that would be lost once the nightly DELETE FROM workspaces cascades every child row away. purge_deadline = request time + 30 days is the product promise; the pg_cron job bunkai-purge-deleted-workspaces (03:00 UTC daily) is its executor.

Flow: Workspace onboarding

  1. User signs up with email/password (or magic link / OAuth GitHub/Google); Supabase Auth creates auth.users with email verification required.
  2. Signed-in browser calls POST /api/v1/workspaces → SECURITY DEFINER RPC bunkai_bootstrap_workspace. Actor is bound from the session (ADR-0012: no caller-supplied actor).
  3. One transaction: workspace row (plan = community, trimmed name, minimum length 1 — SQLSTATE 22023 otherwise), the creator's workspace_members row as owner, a default project, and an activity_log workspace.created entry.
  4. Response carries the new workspace; UI activates it via POST /me/active-workspace.

Business rules: first member is always owner; ownership is transferred, never invited; the bootstrap RPC must never accept a client-declared actor id.

Code paths: app/api/v1/auth/*, app/api/v1/workspaces/route.ts, app/api/v1/me/active-workspace/route.ts.

Flow: Authentication & authorization (dual mode → single Principal)

  1. Two entry rails: browser session (password / magic link / OAuth → Supabase auth cookies) and PAT (bk_pat_… Bearer tokens) for CLI/agents.
  2. Every request resolves to one Principal {userId, workspaceId?, role}; the route layer never branches authorization logic by mode.
  3. Data access is either an RLS-scoped client (session policy path) or a SECURITY DEFINER RPC whose actor is derived server-side (PAT path; a user JWT is minted so auth.uid() applies). ADR-0012.
  4. Raw secrets (PAT, magic-link, invite tokens) live in *_secrets companion tables, revoked from the QA inspector role (0086).
  5. Some routes are structurally cookie-only (e.g. active-workspace switch, membership deletion, data export) and reject Bearer PATs at the gateway.

Business rules: Postgres RLS + RPC actor binding are the authorization source of truth; app-layer checks are defense in depth. Non-disclosure rule: check-email/resend endpoints return uniform responses so errors never leak whether an email exists. Leaving or deleting a workspace revokes the member's PATs.

Code paths: middleware.ts, lib/api/principal.ts, lib/api/middleware/bearer.ts, app/api/v1/me/, app/api/v1/tokens/, app/api/v1/auth/.

Flow: Jira import

  1. QA pastes Jira credentials + JQL into the UI → POST /api/v1/imports creates an import_jobs row (queued; one active job per workspace enforced by 0020) and returns 202 + jobId immediately.
  2. Heavy work runs in a Vercel after() background callback — the HTTP response never waits for Jira paging.
  3. The worker pages Jira's search API, upserts user_stories (with ACs parsed from AC-shaped text) keyed by issue for idempotent re-runs, resolving the target module by path/label rules.
  4. Progress (cursor, counts) is written back per page; the UI polls GET /api/v1/imports/[id] until terminal.
  5. Terminal state emits activity_log import.completed | import.failed.

Business rules: import is idempotent-ish per issue key (upsert) so a re-run does not duplicate stories; failure mid-way leaves failed with partial data — the business accepts partial import + re-run; Jira credentials are used transiently and never echoed back.

Code paths: app/api/v1/imports/route.ts (after() worker), app/api/v1/imports/[id]/route.ts.

Flow: ATC authoring

  1. Author picks layer (UI|API|Unit), optional technique/priority, tags (≤10), ordered steps and assertions, and binds ACs — one call to POST /api/v1/atcs.
  2. The SECURITY DEFINER RPC writes ATC + steps + assertions + AC-bindings transactionally; the atcs_refresh_tsv trigger maintains search_vector for title/tag search.
  3. Edits carry version (optimistic lock): mismatch → 409, forcing the second editor to reload rather than silently clobber.
  4. Duplication copies steps/assertions/AC-binds with fresh identity; GET /atcs/[id]/usage reports which Tests chain this ATC (drives RESTRICT-delete messaging).

Business rules: layer is required (a test must declare where it runs); tags ≤10 and non-empty; atcs.status is not settable by writers (dead column — live verdicts come from run_atcs); deleting an ATC referenced by test_steps is rejected.

Code paths: app/api/v1/atcs/route.ts, atcs/[id]/route.ts, atcs/search/, atcs/[id]/usage/.

Flow: Module tree management

  1. Modules are created under a parent (parentId = null = root) via POST /api/v1/projects/[id]/modules; the RPC computes subtree depth and rejects anything beyond 6 (45xxx family).
  2. Renames/moves recompute the materialized slash-separated path of the whole subtree atomically.
  3. Archive is soft (archived_at) via bunkai_archive_module_subtree, which cascades to descendant modules, their user stories, acceptance criteria and ATCs — it does not cascade to tests or bugs.

Business rules: depth cap 6 is a product decision (UI navigability) enforced in DB; archived subtrees are excluded from pickers but retained for history and bug FKs; module_id on bugs is never null, so module history must remain answerable.

Code paths: app/api/v1/projects/[id]/modules/route.ts, modules/[id]/route.ts.

Flow: Acceptance criteria management

  1. ACs are appended/inserted with explicit position inside their story (POST /api/v1/user-stories/[id]/acceptance-criteria).
  2. user_stories.status moves draft → ready_to_test only through an explicit transition and only when ≥1 active AC exists (SQLSTATE 45xxx family otherwise; gate implemented in 0018).
  3. Archiving an AC through the archive RPC soft-deletes it (archived_at), closes the position gap, and — if it was the last active AC — reverts the parent story to draft inside the same RPC (0017/0018). There is no table-level trigger for this; the revert lives in the SECURITY DEFINER RPC.
  4. AC↔ATC bindings (atc_acceptance_criteria) are managed from the ATC side and surfaced by traceability reports.

Business rules: a story cannot enter ready_to_test with zero testable conditions; archiving never destroys (archived_at only); all app write paths go through the RPCs, so no product code path can bypass the revert.

Code paths: app/api/v1/user-stories/[id]/acceptance-criteria/route.ts, app/api/v1/acceptance-criteria/[id]/route.ts.

Flow: Test authoring

  1. Creating a Test = naming it + ordering existing ATCs (POST /api/v1/tests): the RPC inserts tests + N test_steps rows transactionally (version = 1).
  2. Reorder (POST /tests/[id]/reorder) rewrites all positions in one transaction behind the version lock.
  3. Tags are a text[] column, trimmed/deduped app-side; title trimmed to 1–200.
  4. Deleting an ATC that sits in any chain is refused — the author must first remove it from those chains (usage endpoint shows where).

Business rules: a Test is a view over ATCs, not a copy — chain edits are metadata-only and ATC content changes flow through automatically (why Runs snapshot instead); the same ATC may appear at multiple positions; Tests are workspace-scoped and may chain ATCs from any project in the workspace.

Code paths: app/api/v1/tests/route.ts, tests/[id]/route.ts, tests/[id]/reorder/, tests/tags/, tests/search/.

Flow: Test run execution

  1. Start: POST /api/v1/runs with a client startToken — the RPC's 24h idempotency on (test_id, start_token) makes a retried create return the same Run. Snapshot happens here: test_steps → run_steps, chain ATCs → run_atcs (status = pending), Run inserted running, activity_log run.started.
  2. Execute: POST /runs/[id]/steps/[stepId]/mark updates one step (pending → passed|failed|blocked) and recomputes the parent run_atcs verdict; Realtime pushes the change to subscribed UIs.
  3. Finish: POST /runs/[id]/finish {verdict} flips runs.status to passed|failed, force-skips leftover pending steps → skipped, logs run.finished (with a free-text via channel descriptor), and the activity_log_notify_run_event trigger fans out in-app notifications.
  4. Or abort: POST /runs/[id]/abort {reason} (reason trimmed 3–500) sets aborted + abort_reason; or the pg_cron sweep (*/15 * * * *) closes runs idle >4 minutes with abort_reason = 'Auto-closed by inactivity sweep…' and activity payload via = 'sweep'.
  5. Terminal guards: once terminal, every later finish/abort/mark is rejected (45204/45206/45212) — first terminal wins.

Business rules: run history is immutable; startToken idempotency exists because CLI/agents retry; the free-text via descriptor distinguishes human-caused vs sweep-caused terminals for flake analytics (sweep aborts must not look like QA aborts); only Runs flagged with module_id participate in module-scoped rollups.

Code paths: app/api/v1/runs/route.ts, runs/[id]/finish/, runs/[id]/abort/, runs/[id]/steps/[stepId]/mark/, tests/[id]/runs/ (terminal-only list).

Flow: Bug lifecycle

  1. File: from a failed run step the UI pre-populates provenance; POST /api/v1/bugs → RPC inserts with status = open (the only entry point for status), title trimmed 5–200, ≤10 evidence URLs, module_id mandatory. activity_log bug.filed is logged but does not notify — the run terminal event already did.
  2. Provenance freeze: run_id/run_step_id/atc_id are written once and ON DELETE SET NULL — if the upstream Run/ATC is later purged, the bug keeps its module but loses the link. Frozen semantics: no cascade that would orphan module attribution, no RESTRICT that would block cleanup.
  3. Assign: POST /bugs/[id]/assign (self-assign allowed) → bug.assigned → DB trigger notifies the new assignee.
  4. Transition: POST /bugs/[id]/status moves strictly forward one stage at a time — skipping (45310) and going backward (45311) are rejected. bug.status_changed notifies reporter + assignee (minus the actor).
  5. Consistency backstop: the bugs_check_consistency trigger (SECURITY DEFINER) re-validates cross-references even if a write bypasses the RPC — a cross-tenant or status-invalid bug cannot be inserted by any path.

Business rules: severity P1–P4 is set at filing and changeable through the transition path; bugs are never archived (0061) — the table only grows; forward-only lifecycle means a fixed-then-reopened defect is a new bug (QA links them by convention) — a deliberate choice to keep the state machine auditable.

Code paths: app/api/v1/bugs/route.ts, bugs/[id]/status/, bugs/[id]/assign/, projects/[id]/bugs/, projects/[id]/bugs/heatmap/.

Flow: Notifications inbox & preferences

  1. Business events append to activity_log; AFTER INSERT triggers (activity_log_notify_bug_event, activity_log_notify_run_event) decide whether that event family notifies.
  2. The notify RPC expands eligible recipients, consults notification_preferences (event_type × channel, global per user), and inserts one notifications row per recipient — idempotent on (source_event_id, recipient).
  3. UI inbox pages through GET /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/notifications (cursor + unread count, 90-day window, availability flag); read-state flips are plain RLS UPDATEs (PUT /notifications/[id]/read, POST .../read-all).
  4. Preference edits go through the race-safe upsert RPC; the mentions row cannot be turned off.
  5. Realtime updates the bell badge live.

Business rules: notifications are best-effort presentation of the audit trail, never a second source of truth; 90-day visibility is retention hygiene, not deletion; DB-level idempotency is what makes trigger re-fires safe.

Flow: Daily email digest

  1. Vercel cron hits /api/v1/admin/send-digest at 08:00 UTC; the route accepts GET and POST and authenticates with CRON_SECRET (both verbs because Vercel and manual probes differ).
  2. The candidates RPC claims one notification_digest_log row per user/day (pending, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING): this claim ledger makes cron retries harmless.
  3. TypeScript groups the user's unread notifications, renders the email body, sends via Resend, then marks the claim sent or failed (with error text).
  4. A crash between claim and send leaves a pending row — the next day is a new row (per-day ledger), so at most a delayed digest, never a duplicate-day blast.

Business rules: digest is opt-out per notification_preferences.email × event_type; email sending lives in app code (Vercel), not Postgres — no DB egress by design; the digest is read-only over notifications and creates no new notification rows.

Flow: Billing upgrade (Stripe)

  1. Workspace owner opens billing settings; POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/billing/checkout inserts a billing_checkout_sessions row in open (partial unique: one open per workspace → second click gets 409).
  2. The route creates the Stripe Checkout Session (plan cloud, seat quantity) and back-fills the Stripe session id.
  3. User pays on Stripe; Stripe calls POST /api/v1/billing/webhook. Signature verified against the raw body first.
  4. The handler inserts the Stripe event id into stripe_webhook_events — PK conflict = duplicate delivery = immediate 200, no reprocessing.
  5. For a paid checkout.session.completed, the SECURITY DEFINER RPC applies the upgrade transactionally: workspaces.plan = 'cloud', purchased_seats = seat_quantity, checkout row → completed, audit workspace.plan_upgraded.
  6. Cancel path flips the open row to canceled without touching the plan.

Business rules: plans in play: community (3 projects) → cloud (50) → enterprise (unlimited); limits are DB mirrors of lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts — the DB is authoritative; seat count is purchased metadata only (no invite-time seat gate yet); no subscription lifecycle table — upgrade is a one-shot state change; webhook failure behavior: non-2xx → Stripe retries with backoff (the event-id fence makes retries safe); a lost event means plan not applied until manual backfill.

Flow: Data export

  1. Only the workspace owner, only via cookie session (PAT rejected — exports are browser-grade actions), and only one active export at a time: POST /api/v1/workspaces/[id]/data-export inserts a queued row.
  2. The insert trigger appends activity_log export.requested (audit of who pulled data out).
  3. A Vercel after() worker (service-role client — RLS on this table is owner-SELECT-only) flips running, gathers the tenant's rows, builds the archive, uploads it to the Storage bucket workspace-exports, then completed (+ expires_at = completed_at + 168h) or failed with error text.
  4. Download re-checks fresh owner membership + completed + not expired, resolves through the RPC, streams the archive, and logs export.downloaded.

Business rules: 168-hour (7-day) archive lifetime — long enough to hand off, short enough that a leaked URL ages out; export is read-only over tenant data; worker crash can strand a row in running (no auto-requeue observed).

Flow: Workspace deletion, restore & purge

  1. Owner-only soft delete: DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/[id] → RPC stamps deleted_at, revokes every member PAT and pending invite (same transaction — no window where tokens outlive intent), captures row_count_digest, upserts the workspace_deletions tombstone with purge_deadline = now() + 30 days, logs workspace.deleted and returns the recipients list.
  2. The route's after() sends the courtesy email via Resend to all members (“deleted, restore in 30d”).
  3. Restore exists for the whole grace window (POST /workspaces/[id]/restore): clears deleted_at and the tombstone, logs workspace.restored — soft delete is a recoverable mistake for 30 days, then irreversible.
  4. At 03:00 UTC the pg_cron job bunkai-purge-deleted-workspaces hard-deletes expired tenants (DELETE FROM workspaces → CASCADE wipes projects/modules/stories/ATCs/runs/bugs…), then stamps purged_at on the tombstone — the tombstone deliberately outlives the tenant (no FK to workspaces).

Business rules: the 30-day grace is the product promise (the email says so) and the cron is its executor; PAT/invite revocation happens at request time, not purge time; the tombstone keeps member_count + row_count_digest for compliance; no admin veto/hold path was found.

Flow: Milestone tracking

  1. A milestone is created with a name (1–100 chars), optional description (≤500) and an optional target_date via POST /api/v1/projects/[id]/milestones.
  2. Date validation runs on create and on change: today ≤ target_date ≤ today + 5 years; an unchanged date is never re-validated (historical milestones do not start failing).
  3. Duplicate names inside a project → 409 (DB unique index).

Business rules: milestones are date markers, not workflow objects — no status, no completion state, no archive/delete, deliberately deferred (0064); they anchor release-planning views and future test-plan correlation.

Flow: Coverage & traceability reporting

  1. Coverage: for each module/AC, join atc_acceptance_criteria × latest run_atcs.status — executed verdicts come from run_atcs, never from the dead atcs.status column (0050 documented this decoupling).
  2. Traceability: one SECURITY DEFINER statement walks Story → AC → ATC → Test → Run → Defect — the audit view QA leads sign off on.
  3. Recovery cycles: time from a bug's filed → resolved transitions, per module/severity — feeds flake/quality trend charts.
  4. Run reports are split by semantics: the test-runs list RPC returns terminal-only runs with filter-invariant totals, while the project-runs report includes running and is filter-reactive — filters must agree with totals or QA loses trust.

Business rules: reporting is read-only and RPC-mediated (aggregates never leak through direct table reads); dead-column discipline: any report reading atcs.status is a bug.

State machine: User story status

From To Event Effects
draft ready_to_test Explicit transition with ≥1 active AC Story enters QA scope; 45xxx error if 0 active ACs (gate fn 0018).
ready_to_test draft Last active AC archived (inside the archive RPC, 0017/0018) Story auto-reverts in the same transaction; no product write path can bypass the RPCs.

Soft-archive is orthogonal: archived_at hides a story without destroying it.

State machine: Run, run step and ATC verdict

From To Event Effects
— running POST /runs (24h (test_id, start_token) idempotency) Snapshots run_atcs/run_steps; activity_log run.started.
running passed POST /runs/[id]/finish (via channel descriptor optional) Leftover pending run_steps → skipped; run.finished → notify trigger.
running failed Same finish RPC, failed verdict Same side effects; coverage rollups pick it up.
running aborted POST /runs/[id]/abort {reason} OR pg_cron sweep (idle >4 min, via = 'sweep' in activity payload) abort_reason stored (CHECK-coherent with status); sweep-vs-human distinguished for flake analytics.
Terminal Terminal (any) Late finish/abort/mark Rejected (45204/45206/45212) — history immutable, first terminal wins.

Run step (sub-machine):

From To Event Effects
pending passed/failed/blocked POST /runs/[id]/steps/[stepId]/mark Recomputes parent run_atcs verdict; Realtime push.
pending skipped Run finish/abort (bulk) Unmarked work is closed out, not left dangling.
Terminal — Late mark Rejected (pending-only guard, 45213 family).

Run ATC verdict (computed, not authored): any step pending → pending; else any failed → failed; else any blocked → blocked; else all passed → passed. Recomputed inside the step-mark RPC on every mark; never an independent write target. There is no created Run state (rows insert as running), and no runs.via column — via is a free-text channel descriptor on the terminal RPCs, stored in the activity_log payload.

State machine: Bug status (forward-only)

From To Event Effects
— open POST /bugs Provenance frozen (SET NULL on upstream delete); bug.filed logged, no notify.
open in_progress POST /bugs/[id]/status bug.status_changed → notify reporter+assignee (minus actor).
in_progress resolved Same transition RPC Same notify fan-out; severity/assignee unchanged by the transition itself.
resolved closed Same Terminal in practice — reopening is DB-blocked (forward-only): a regression is a new bug.
Any Non-successor Attempt Rejected: 45311 (backward) / 45310 (skip ahead).

Entry point for status is create only (open); the bugs_check_consistency trigger is the backstop against writes that bypass the RPCs. There is no rejected state in the schema.

State machine: Import job

From To Event Effects
queued running Vercel after() worker picks up the job Pages Jira; writes stories+ACs incrementally; progress cursor updated per page.
running completed JQL exhausted activity_log import.completed; UI stops polling.
running failed Jira error / credential failure Partial stories remain (accepted partial import + re-run via upsert).

One active import job per workspace (0020). A worker crash can strand a row in running (no requeue observed).

State machine: Billing checkout session

From To Event Effects
open completed Webhook checkout.session.completed (paid, event-id fenced) workspaces.plan = 'cloud', purchased_seats set, audit workspace.plan_upgraded.
open canceled POST .../checkout/cancel Plan untouched.
open expired Stripe expiry New checkout attempt allowed (frees the one-open slot).
Terminal — Second open attempt while one is open 409 (partial unique) — prevents double Stripe sessions.

State machine: Workspace export

From To Event Effects
queued running after() worker starts Export row is the job queue (one active export enforced app-side).
running completed Archive built + uploaded to workspace-exports bucket expires_at = completed_at + 168h armed; download RPC unlocks.
running failed Build/upload error Error text stored; user may re-request (no auto-requeue).
completed (expired) expires_at passes Download RPC refuses; archive reaped.

State machine: Workspace lifecycle (soft delete → restore / purge)

From To Event Effects
Active Soft-deleted Owner DELETE /workspaces/[id] deleted_at set; PATs + invites revoked; tombstone purge_deadline = +30d; Resend notice to members.
Soft-deleted Active POST /workspaces/[id]/restore within grace deleted_at cleared; tombstone removed; audit workspace.restored.
Soft-deleted Purged pg_cron bunkai-purge-deleted-workspaces (03:00 UTC, ≥30d) DELETE workspaces → CASCADE all tenant rows; tombstone purged_at stamped and stays.

State machine: Membership role/status & invites

Roles form a hierarchy viewer < member < admin < owner; invites may only carry viewer | member | admin (ownership is transferred, never invited). Membership status is active | invited | suspended — only active unlocks RLS data access.

From To Event Effects
Member Owner Ownership transfer Previous owner demoted; never two owners, never zero.
Any Removed Leave / kicked / workspace deleted Member's PATs revoked in the same transaction as the removal.
pending invite Accepted Invitee authenticates + accepts within 7 days Membership row created at the invited role.
pending invite Expired / revoked 7-day TTL / owner revoke / workspace soft-delete Token unusable (secrets companion row killed too).

State machine: Email digest claim

From To Event Effects
— pending Cron candidates RPC (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) Claim = duplicate-blast protection; one row per user per calendar day.
pending sent Resend attempt succeeds in the digest route Daily digest delivered; row is the audit record.
pending failed Resend attempt errors Error text stored; visible for ops; next digest is a new day's row (no same-day retry storm).

Test-plan lifecycle (test_plans.status ∈ open|closed) is CHECK-verified; Close is the sole exit and no delete path exists (0073 design decision).

Automatic processes

Database triggers

Trigger Fires on What it does Why it exists
atcs_set_updated_at, tests_set_updated_at, runs_set_updated_at, bugs_set_updated_at, milestones_set_updated_at, test_plans_set_updated_at, notification_preferences_set_updated_at, notification_digest_log_set_updated_at UPDATE of the respective table Refresh updated_at Audit freshness regardless of which writer path ran.
atcs_refresh_tsv INSERT/UPDATE atcs Rebuild search_vector (title/tags) ATC search must be instant and consistent without app-side indexing.
bunkai_enforce_project_limit_trigger BEFORE INSERT projects Plan ladder: community = 3, cloud = 50, enterprise = ∞ (SQLSTATE 45700) Monetization boundary lives in the DB — no app deployment can forget the limit.
bugs_check_consistency INSERT/UPDATE bugs SECURITY DEFINER backstop: re-validate provenance/scope/status/assignee invariants RPCs are the front door, the trigger is the ceiling — even a bypassing write cannot create a cross-tenant or status-invalid bug.
activity_log_notify_bug_event AFTER INSERT activity_log (bug actions) Expand recipients → notifications (idempotent) Inbox fan-out belongs in the DB: no app worker can forget an event.
activity_log_notify_run_event AFTER INSERT activity_log (run terminal) Same, for run lifecycle events Run results must reach the team even if the originating tab closed.
workspace_exports_log_requested AFTER INSERT workspace_exports activity_log export.requested Data-egress audit: someone pulled a tenant archive.

The last-active-AC story revert is not a table trigger: it lives inside the SECURITY DEFINER archive RPCs (0017/0018). All product write paths go through those RPCs, so the business guarantee holds, but a raw SQL bypass of the RPC would not revert the story (see discovery-gaps).

Cron jobs

Job Schedule What it does Why it exists
bunkai-sweep-abandoned-runs (pg_cron, 0075) */15 * * * * Runs with no step activity for >4 min → aborted, reason 'Auto-closed by inactivity sweep…', activity payload via = 'sweep'; leftover pending steps → skipped A crashed browser must not leave runs running forever — they would poison coverage metrics and the live UI.
bunkai-purge-deleted-workspaces (pg_cron, 0084) 0 3 * * * (03:00 UTC) Hard-delete tenants soft-deleted ≥30d; stamp tombstone purged_at Executes the 30-day deletion promise at a low-traffic hour; tombstone survives for compliance.
Email digest (Vercel cron, vercel.json) 0 8 * * * (08:00 UTC) GET+POST /api/v1/admin/send-digest gated by CRON_SECRET → claim ledger → Resend Daily unread digest; per-day claim row makes cron retries harmless.

Webhooks

Direction Endpoint Payload → effect Why it exists
Inbound (Stripe) POST /api/v1/billing/webhook Stripe event → HMAC signature check on raw body → stripe_webhook_events PK fence → apply plan = 'cloud' + seats via service-role RPC Payment confirmation cannot rely on the browser returning from checkout — the payment provider is the source of truth.
Outbound — None (no Bunkai-originated webhooks configured) —

Vercel after() background workers (neither cron nor webhooks): the Jira import runner (POST /imports — HTTP must return 202 immediately; Jira paging takes minutes), the data-export builder (archive assembly must not block the request), and the deletion-notice email sender (Postgres has no egress — email must originate in app code, a design constraint, not an oversight). No Supabase Edge Functions exist (supabase/functions empty) — all server logic runs in Next.js route handlers.

Integration: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Realtime + Storage)

  • Data: all tenant state. RLS is the authorization source of truth (app checks are advisory); every mutation that fans out goes through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs with server-bound actors (ADR-0012).
  • Realtime: run_atcs and run_steps are in the supabase_realtime publication (0043); notifications updates the inbox badge live. Subscribers only receive rows they could already SELECT (Realtime enforces RLS).
  • Storage: bucket workspace-exports holds export archives for 168 hours.
  • Dependent flows: every flow in this document.
  • Failure behavior: DB down → all writes fail closed (5xx); no partial-apply risk because mutations are single RPC transactions. Realtime loss → UI shows stale verdicts until reconnect (business tolerates — the DB is correct).
  • QA access: a dedicated read-only role qa_inspector_ro exists for DBHub analysis; 0086 revoked its secret-table access.

Integration: Jira (Cloud)

  • Data: issues → user stories + acceptance criteria (one-way import). external_id/external_url carry the external link; one active story per (project_id, upper(external_id)).
  • Dependent flows: Jira import; module mapping rules decide placement.
  • Failure: auth/JQL error → import_jobs.status = 'failed', partial rows kept, user re-runs (upsert = safe re-entry). Credentials used transiently, never echoed.
  • Direction: read-only from Bunkai's perspective — no webhooks in, no status pushes out. Bidirectional sync is not implemented.

Integration: Stripe

  • Data: plan state (community → cloud), purchased_seats, checkout attempt rows; webhook events fenced by event id.
  • Dependent flows: billing upgrade; the project-limit trigger switches 3 → 50 on plan flip.
  • Failure: webhook non-2xx → Stripe retries (fence = idempotent); signature mismatch → rejected with no state change; lost event → plan not applied until manual backfill (no poller exists). Missing Stripe config → checkout returns 503 payment_processor_unavailable; the rest of the app boots without Stripe (lazy client).

Integration: Resend (email)

  • Data: rendered digest bodies and deletion-notice emails. No templates DB-side; sending lives in app code (Postgres has no egress by design).
  • Dependent flows: daily email digest; workspace-deletion courtesy notice.
  • Failure: Resend outage → digest claim marked failed (row retained, no same-day retry storm); deletion email lost but the tombstone/restore path is unaffected (email is courtesy, not mechanism). Missing API key degrades digest sends per-user without crashing the app.

Integration: Vercel (hosting + cron + workers)

  • Data: none of its own; it executes app logic and schedules it (digest cron; after() workers for import, export and deletion email).
  • Dependent flows: Jira import, email digest, data export, workspace-deletion notice.
  • Failure: cron misconfigured/removed → digest silently stops (claim rows simply do not appear); after() lost on a cold crash → export or import stuck running (the status columns are the observable signal). Locally, cron never fires — tests must trigger the digest route directly with CRON_SECRET.

Discovery gaps

Everything that could not be verified, plus drift between the legacy map (input) and the current schema (checked 2026-10-10 against supabase/migrations/ + app/ in upex-bunkai-tms).

Open gaps

  • Overview figures deferred: diagram-design style gate not resolved (no .diagram-design marker).
  • Live DB schema was not queried in this pass (migrations + app code only, no DB MCP) — live-vs-migrations drift and live pg_policies/pg_trigger/pg_cron.job state remain unverified.
  • Live API was not exercised; all route behavior is inferred from code and the OpenAPI contract.
  • feature_flags runtime usage: table exists (scope global|workspace); no consumer traced.
  • user_view_state write path and shape not re-verified beyond schema presence.
  • Seat enforcement: purchased_seats is display metadata; no invite-time seat gate exists (follow-up, not a bug).
  • Workspace deletion: no admin-hold/veto path found — confirm intentional.
  • Export/import workers can strand rows in running if the after() callback dies (no requeue observed).
  • SQLSTATE 45308 allocated twice (0051 + 0052) and 45203 reserved but unimplemented (0037) — code-hygiene issues inherited from the legacy map's observations, not re-verified this pass.
  • Realtime end-to-end behavior (two-session empirical verification) was called out as still required by migration 0043 itself; only the publication + client channel file existence were verified here.
  • Resend template/HTML specifics, bounce handling, and the exact deletion-notice copy were not read line-by-line.
  • Vercel cron history and after() runtime behavior unobserved (config read only).

Drift found (legacy map vs current schema, 2026-10-10)

  • Last-AC auto-revert: the legacy map describes a “DB trigger” that reverts the story to draft. Current schema implements the revert inside the SECURITY DEFINER archive RPCs (0017/0018) — there is no table-level trigger on acceptance_criteria. Business guarantee holds for all RPC-mediated writes; a raw SQL bypass would not revert.
  • runs.via user|sweep: there is no via column on runs. via is a free-text channel descriptor parameter on the finish/abort RPCs (0067), stored verbatim in the activity_log payload; the inactivity sweep writes via = 'sweep' only into that payload (0075).
  • Legacy open gap closed: test_plans are project-scoped (0073), with unique (project_id, lower(name)), SELECT-only RLS and DEFINER-RPC-only writes — not workspace-scoped.
  • Infra-map gap partially stale: the “Supabase Realtime push not confirmed” note predates 0043 verification — run_atcs/run_steps ARE in the supabase_realtime publication and the client channel (lib/runs/realtime-run-channel.ts) exists. UI-level behavior still awaits empirical verification (0043's own requirement).
  • ATC classification (0087) enumerations were not in the legacy map: technique = Equivalence Partitioning | Boundary Value Analysis | State Transition | Decision Table | Pairwise; priority = Critical | High | Medium | Low; both nullable, never defaulted. Enrichment, not conflict.
  • Dead-column value set precision: atcs.status CHECK is pass|fail|blocked|skipped|running|unrun (non-past-tense), distinct from run step/verdict statuses pending|passed|failed|blocked|skipped — both confirmed; the legacy map carried this correctly.

Verified closes (legacy gaps resolved this pass)

  • Bootstrap RPC name handling: trimmed, minimum length 1 (SQLSTATE 22023) — 0006.
  • Invite TTL: expires_at defaults to now() + interval '7 days' — 0010.
  • Notification visibility: 90-day filter enforced in the list RPC (created_at >= now() - interval '90 days') — 0053.
  • Project environments: Staging + Production seeded once for projects existing at 0031; default-deny writes; no re-seed for new projects — 0031.
  • Sweep schedule and threshold: */15 * * * *, idle >4 minutes, reason prefix 'Auto-closed by inactivity sweep:' — 0075.
  • Purge schedule and grace: 0 3 * * *, deleted_at <= now() - interval '30 days' — 0084.
